name: Theological vs Secular Ethics

objectives.text: Identify that the Bible teaches God is good and tells people what is right and wrong
Name the Ten Commandments as the rules God gave his people to show them how to live
Retell how Jesus summarized God's law as loving God and loving your neighbor
Describe how Romans 2 explains that people who do not know the Bible still have a sense of right and wrong written on their hearts
Explain that secular ethics is an approach that decides right and wrong without reference to God or Scripture
Explain why the Bible teaches that every human life has worth because people are made in the image of God
Compare a reason for an action based on God's command with a reason based on personal feeling or preference
Identify common secular sources of moral authority such as personal feelings, cultural agreement, civil law, and human well-being
Apply the Ten Commandments to contemporary moral situations using the catechism's account of what each commandment requires and forbids
Explain the Euthyphro dilemma and the Reformed response that goodness is grounded in God's unchanging nature rather than in arbitrary will or a standard above God
Explain the moral argument for God's existence and identify its premises and conclusion
Analyze how Christian and secular accounts each ground human dignity and human rights, including the biblical teaching on the image of God
Explain individual and cultural moral relativism and identify the internal tensions in each form
Explain how the Reformed tradition accounts for real moral goodness in the actions of those who do not believe, while distinguishing it from works done in faith
Construct an argument for objective moral standards that draws on Scripture and the tradition's teaching that the moral law binds all people
Evaluate evolutionary accounts that explain morality as a product of survival and social instinct
Evaluate major objections to divine command theory and distinguish it from the Reformed view of the moral law as a perfect rule of righteousness reflecting God's character
Analyze how Scripture and the Reformed confessions relate law and love, including love as the fulfilling of the law and the uses of the law for believers
Create a comparative analysis of a contemporary ethical issue showing how a theological and a secular framework each reach and justify their conclusions

changes: Reworded K and grade 1 objectives to anchor them in Scripture and the catechism. Dropped 'doing good makes God happy' and 'why we need God to have real rules' as vague or as duplicates of later objectives. Added the summary of the law (grade 2), the image of God (grade 4), secular sources of moral authority (grade 6), and the Reformed account of moral goodness among unbelievers (grade 10). Paired the Euthyphro dilemma with the Reformed answer grounded in God's nature, and kept divine command theory as a distinct evaluation at grade 11. Widened the grade 12 law and love objective to include the uses of the law, and added a capstone comparative analysis. Left the named ethical systems to the sibling sub-topic. Replaced the cited references where better anchors existed, and left anchors empty where no text truly states the competency.
